# test_title_case.py
import pytest

from your_module import title_case  # Replace "your_module" with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_text, expected",
    [
        ("hello world", "Hello World"),
        ("the quick brown fox", "The Quick Brown Fox"),
        ("PYTHON IS FUN", "Python Is Fun"),
        ("mIxEd CaSe WoRdS", "Mixed Case Words"),
        ("already Title Case", "Already Title Case"),
    ],
)
def test_title_case_happy_path(input_text, expected):
    assert title_case(input_text) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_text, expected",
    [
        ("", ""),
        ("   ", ""),
        (" hello ", "Hello"),
        ("hello   world", "Hello World"),
        ("\thello\tworld\t", "Hello World"),
        ("hello\nworld", "Hello World"),
        ("hello\r\nworld", "Hello World"),
    ],
)
def test_title_case_whitespace_edge_cases(input_text, expected):
    assert title_case(input_text) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_text, expected",
    [
        ("123 abc", "123 Abc"),
        ("hello-world", "Hello-world"),
        ("o'CONNOR", "O'connor"),
        ("éLAN vital", "Élan Vital"),
        ("hello, world!", "Hello, World!"),
    ],
)
def test_title_case_special_characters(input_text, expected):
    assert title_case(input_text) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "invalid_input",
    [
        None,
        123,
        ["hello", "world"],
        {"text": "hello world"},
    ],
)
def test_title_case_invalid_non_string_inputs_raise_attribute_error(invalid_input):
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        title_case(invalid_input)


def test_title_case_bytes_input_raises_type_error():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        title_case(b"hello world")
